The test image shows a soybean leaf with:
- Dense, dark brown/reddish-brown angular spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Yellowish-orange discoloration surrounding lesion clusters
- Concentration at the leaf tip with spots spreading across the blade
- Small to medium-sized spots with angular shape following leaf vein patterns

This pattern strongly suggests **Septoria brown spot** — angular red-to-brown spots with surrounding chlorosis. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image shows field-level Septoria (general yellowing/defoliation), while the test image shows a close-up leaf with dense angular dark spots and orange-yellow chlorosis around them. This matches the Septoria description well: "Angular, red to brown spots varying from tiny specks to quarter-inch diameter appear on upper and lower leaf surfaces. Leaves with numerous spots rapidly turn yellow."

The key features aligning with Septoria_brown_spot:
- **Angular dark brown spots** of varying small sizes across the leaf
- **Surrounding yellowish-orange chlorosis** (the classic premature yellowing)
- Dense spot distribution typical of heavy Septoria infection
- Pattern consistent with the "tiny specks to quarter-inch" description
